name: level3-playthrough-ecology
description: Level 3 (Treranium Depths) ecological shutdown scenario: massive krackle and obliviax blasts with no mitigation, long tick cycles to trigger ecology collapse. `campaign start level:treranium_depths` fails outright (tier-3, locked by default -- pre-existing, already documented per Finding #24 in this file's own step descriptions and Finding #58/#59 elsewhere in this doc); runs against the substitute new_game world instead. #553 (drill_hole became a queued, vehicle-gated action) breaks the rest of the named premise for real, not just the depth-mismatch Finding #61 already covered: this file's 6 patterns (5x4/4x5/5x5/5x5/6x5/6x6, 156 holes total -- the largest drilling total of any file in this batch) used to write every hole into state.drillHoles in one frame; now each hole is a queued drill_hole action a licensed driller spends real ticks physically driving a drill_rig to sink, one at a time, before charging/sequencing/blasting (unchanged, still operate on state.drillHoles only) can touch it. staffed:true's own composition costs real ticks too -- five employees and four vehicles' payroll/maintenance/fuel accrue whether or not they ever work. Under those costs, against a starting budget that tops out at $92,800 (staffed:true's free $50,000, plus $42,800 scrapping the debris_hauler/rock_digger/rock_fragmenter this blast-only file never uses) with zero income anywhere in the file (no contracts, ever), this pass measured -- exhaustively, across paired vs. single drill_rig crews, immediate vs. deferred hiring, with and without the fleet scrap, with and without a relocate-before-blast maneuver that saves the rig from its own blast -- that the mine cannot survive past its first blast's aftermath. BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS (100, Bankruptcy.ts) always runs out before a second pattern can be drilled with a single-driller pace this budget can afford, let alone before three more patterns' worth of blasts (900+ ticks, the pre-#553 file's own requirement to first push ecology to 0) could ever fire. The result: pattern 1 drills and blasts for real (20 holes, krackle, 260-345 ticks single-driller with the 7 hand-hires deferred to mid-drilling for cash reasons; 4 of 12 employees die; ecology crashes 50 -> 29.54; the drill_rig survives a deliberate relocate before firing). Pattern 2 orders its 20 holes for free but never drills a single one -- no licensed, equipped driller survives the budget to work it -- and the mine goes bankrupt at tick 369 attempting it. Patterns 3-6 are never reached at all: continuing to narrate drill_plan cycles nothing can ever staff past a game-over state would document nothing real. levelEndReason is 'bankruptcy', not 'ecological_shutdown' -- the named premise's ending no longer holds, exactly the class of finding Finding #24 already established elsewhere in this file (the named thing doesn't happen; here is what really does, re-measured and asserted exactly).

steps.description: #553: staffed:true's four vehicles all come unmanned (driverId:null) -- this crews the free drill_rig with the staffed driller (employee #1) before anything can drill. Panel opened once here; every later vehicle step in this file reuses it already open.

Finding: this file is pure blast-only (no contracts, no hauling, no rock clearing anywhere in it, per the pre-#553 pass's own note) -- the debris_hauler/rock_digger/rock_fragmenter staffed:true grants are dead weight the moment the game opens, and under #553 that weight is no longer free: drill_hole is now a queued action a driller spends real ticks on, and this file's 6 patterns (156 holes total, the largest in this batch) need a very long drilling window before their first blast can even fire. VEHICLE_SCRAP_RESIDUAL_FRACTION is 0.4 (balance.ts) and these three are still at full HP, so scrapping them back for $10,000 + $20,000 + $12,800 = $42,800 turns three idle maintenance drains into the cash cushion that keeps the mine solvent through that window -- explored and required; see the tick-block notes below for the arithmetic.
Same finding as the debris_hauler scrap above -- rock_digger never does anything in this file either.
Same finding -- rock_fragmenter is the third and last unused staffed vehicle; only the drill_rig (vehicle #1) is ever driven in this file.

campaign start level:treranium_depths FAILS at step 1 ("Level treranium_depths is locked. Complete previous levels first." -- Campaign.ts unlocks only tier-1 levels by default, treranium_depths is tier 3) -- a real, pre-existing scenario bug predating #553 (Finding #24), untouched by this pass. Every subsequent command runs against whatever the substitute new_game seed:3666 staffed:true produced instead of the intended level.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:5 cols:4 spacing:3 depth:6 diameter:0.089 start:10,10
steps.description: #553: confirming the grid only orders the 20 holes -- they are ghosts until a licensed driller drives the drill_rig to each one, so holeCount is 0 here (was 20 pre-#553); the tick blocks below drain the order.

expect.note: #553: sandbox-measured. A single driller (employee #1, the staffed:true composition's only driving.drill_rig licence) lands this 20-hole pattern in 13 tick(20)/event(choose 0) cycles -- 260 ticks -- interspersed with the fatigue-collapse rest cycles Employee.ts's needs system forces on a site with no living_quarters (a real driller collapses and rests in the dirt repeatedly, not just once). The 7 hand-hired employees below are NOT hired yet at this point -- deliberately: cash crosses BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD ($5,000, balance.ts) on its own well before this pattern finishes even with the scrap boost, and BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS is only 100 -- hiring 7 more salaries any earlier than this checkpoint burns the grace period before the first blast can even fire (sandbox-measured: hiring all 7 at tick 0 instead of here bankrupts the mine mid-pattern-1, around tick 220). Hiring here, once the single driller is already 16/20 holes in, is the latest point cash can still afford all seven ($20,138 vs. $8,300 total hiring cost) while leaving the rest of this pattern's drilling window inside the 100-tick grace once the new payroll starts compounding.

Corrected from role guard/command to role player/real clicks (a sibling file in this same batch, level1-playthrough-win.json, found the control this file's first pass missed): `move_here` is a real, player-clickable vehicle action -- select the vehicle, click MOVE HERE in the selection bar that opens (SelectionBar.ts's SelectionAction union) -- so there was never a genuine gap to guard against. The relocate itself is unchanged and still load-bearing: without it, the drill_rig that just finished sinking this pattern is still parked among the very holes about to detonate, and Damage.ts's fragment-hit check (BUILDING_DAMAGE_THRESHOLD 500 kJ, well below what a CATASTROPHIC-rated krackle blast throws at point-blank range) destroys it in the blast that follows -- sandbox-confirmed: skipping this step and firing immediately drops vehicleCount to 0 after the blast below, with no cash left anywhere in this file to buy a replacement rig. Moving the rig off to the side first -- even only 15 ticks' worth of travel at drill_rig's speed 1 (VEHICLE_BASE_STATS, balance.ts), well short of actually reaching (35,35) -- is enough separation that the same blast leaves it standing (sandbox-confirmed: vehicleCount stays 1). The 4 employees this blast kills below are unaffected either way; only the vehicle's survival depends on this step. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): selection swapped from the Fleet-panel-row click (`#bs-toolbar [data-panel="vehicles"]` + `[data-vehicle-id="1"]`) to `clickEntity` (direct scene pick, bypassing the panel): FleetPanel.update() only runs while its panel is visible (UIManager.ts:405), and this file's vehicles panel was last open ~880 steps and ~345 ticks earlier, superseded by the employees panel since -- SelectionBar.show() (SelectionBar.ts:68-76) calls describe() first and hide()s without ever building the move_here button when that describe fails, so the button was never in the DOM to await, not merely slow to appear. Every other file that reaches move_here after a real gap already uses clickEntity for the same reason (nav-move-costs-visual.json, vehicle-task-states-visual.json, nav-dynamic-updates-visual.json); files that keep move_here reachable via the panel instead keep that panel continuously open the whole time (vehicle-traffic.json).

Charge All commits the panel's current product card / amount / stemming (ChargeStep.chargeAll, Charge.ts): the krackle product card selects the explosive, 5 amount increments take 5 -> 10kg (krackle's maximum) and 5 stemming decrements take 2.0 -> 1.0m.
Sequence's delay-step stepper carries data-field="delay-step" (Sequence.ts). 3 decrement clicks: 25ms default -> 20 -> 15 -> 10 (DELAY_STEP_INCREMENT=5ms, Sequence.ts).

This blast fires for real (campaign start's lock, per the Finding above, only means it runs on the substitute new_game world, not that firing is blocked). Finding: 4 of the 12 employees on site die (deathCount 0 -> 4) -- a direct trace of who: employees #1 (Gus Rubble, the driller who just spent 260-345 ticks physically working every hole in this pattern), #2 (Walt Rockwell, the staffed blaster), #3 (Earl Boulder) and #5 (Walt Quartzman, two of the staffed drivers) are all standing close enough to the pattern for Damage.ts's DEATH_THRESHOLD (2000 kJ) to be met; employee #4 (Pete Quartzman) and all 7 hand-hired employees (#6-#12, hired at tick 260 and never dispatched anywhere near the pattern) survive. The drill_rig (vehicle #1) survives too, thanks to the relocate step above. Ecology crashes 50 -> 29.54 (ScoreManager.ts's vibration-based ecology penalty).

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:4 cols:5 spacing:3 depth:6 diameter:0.089 start:25,10
steps.description: Finding #62 (this pass): ordering a plan is free and unrestricted -- drill_plan itself never checks cash or crew, so this still succeeds and queues 20 ghost holes exactly as declared. What changes is everything downstream. Cash is -$62,402 and there is no licensed, equipped driller left: the only driving.drill_rig licence on the roster died with employee #1 in the blast above, none of the 7 hand-hired employees hold it, and licensing one (`employee assign_skill <id> skill:driving.drill_rig level:1`) would not help even if it were free -- there is nothing left to spend on a second vehicle, and the one surviving rig has no living driver to claim it. orderedHoleCount sits at 20 forever; holeCount never leaves the 0 this pattern starts at. This is why this file only ever reaches 2 of its originally-described 6 patterns -- see the file description for the full finding.

Left as a command, guard role, and not reachable by any click sequence for a reason distinct from this file's earlier pre-#553 "invalid amount" findings (patterns 4/6, further down this file's own history): with holeCount at 0, the Drill step never has a single physically-drilled hole to hand off to Charge, so charge-all has nothing to act on and the panel's own step-advance leaves it unreachable -- there is no button a player could click through to a charge. The console has no such gate: createCharge (ChargePlan.ts) charges 0 of the 0 holes that exist, chargedCount stays 0, and the command itself reports success ("Charged 0 holes") rather than throwing.
Same gate as the charge step above -- with 0 drilled holes there is no Sequence tab content to click into. sequence auto reports "0 holes" and sequencedCount stays 0.

Left as a command: with nothing drilled, charged or sequenced there is no Fire step to reach, let alone execute. The command itself does not throw -- it produces a hollow, "BAD"-rated report (0 cleared voxels, 0 fragments, $0 ore value) and leaves every count at 0. No employee is anywhere near a blast that never really happens: deathCount stays at 4, ecology stays at 29.54.

Finding #63 (this pass) -- the file's real ending under #553: cash first crossed BANKRUPTCY_THRESHOLD ($5,000) around tick 280 (see the tick block after the hire above) and has been below it ever since; BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS (100, Bankruptcy.ts) runs out at tick 369, inside this block ("Advanced 20 tick(s)" landing at 380, with the "BANKRUPTCY! The mine is seized." line logged at tick 369). levelEndReason becomes 'bankruptcy', not 'ecological_shutdown': ecology only ever reached 29.54 (this file's one real blast, above) and EcologicalDisaster.ts's shutdown needs ecology <= 0 held for ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS (150) straight -- a threshold this file's economics never let it reach even once, let alone hold. This was tested exhaustively, not assumed: single vs. paired drill_rig crews, hiring the 7 hand-hires immediately vs. deferred, with and without scrapping the unused staffed fleet, with and without the relocate-before-blast maneuver that saves vehicle #1 above -- every combination this pass tried goes bankrupt at or within one pattern of the first blast, because BANKRUPTCY_GRACE_TICKS (~100-370 ticks of runway from a $50,000-$92,800 start with zero income anywhere in this file) is an order of magnitude smaller than the 900+ ticks three more single-driller-paced patterns (the minimum the pre-#553 file needed to first reach ecology<=0) would now cost under #553's queued, vehicle-gated drilling. The named premise ("ecology collapse triggering the ecological shutdown") no longer holds; the mine's own payroll ends it first, the same class of finding as Finding #24's pre-existing locked-level cascade elsewhere in this file's history.
No pending event at this tick -- a safe no-op, same convention as every other event choose 0 step in this file.
